explanation.text: The June 2022 HTTP/1.1 standard, published as RFC 9110 by the IETF, classifies the PUT method as idempotent.
RFC 9110 is an Internet Standard published in June 2022 that defines HTTP semantics, including method properties such as idempotency.
The definition of idempotent methods in RFC 9110 includes PUT, stating that successive identical requests have the same effect as a single request.
RFC 7231, a predecessor specification, also classifies PUT as idempotent, and its classification remains valid in the June 2022 standard.
Supporting excerpts confirm that PUT is explicitly listed as idempotent in authoritative and secondary sources aligned with the June 2022 standard.

The methods PUT and DELETE, and safe methods are defined as idempotent. Safe methods are trivially idempotent, since they are intended to have no effect on the server whatsoever; the PUT and DELETE methods, meanwhile, are idempotent since successive identical requests will be ignored.

excerpts.text: Let's have a look at the [RFC 7231](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7231), the document defines the semantics and the content of the HTTP/1.1 protocol.

> **A request method is considered "idempotent" if the intended effect on the server of multiple identical requests with that method is the same as the effect for a single such request**. Of the request methods defined by this specification, `PUT`, `DELETE`, and safe request methods are idempotent. [...]
